mainTopic: Levels of disqualification for a כהן, and the head, back, eyebrow, eye and nose blemishes of the משנה
overview: The גמרא first sets out three levels of disqualification for a כהן. A real מום profanes the עבודה. A כהן who is שאינו שוה בזרעו של אהרן does not profane it, but he violates a עשה if he serves. A כהן kept out only because of מראית העין breaks no Torah law. Next the גמרא explains the unusual head and neck shapes listed in the משנה, and it narrows the dispute about a hump to a hump with no bone. רבא then gives two versions of which kind of bald כהן is disqualified. רבי יוחנן rules that bald כהנים, dwarves and כהנים with leaky eyes are truly disqualified, and after several challenges the גמרא explains that he is rejecting a ברייתא that follows רבי יהודה. A new משנה defines the גבן, and the גמרא reconciles it with a ברייתא and explains that 'two spines' means a crooked spine. A final משנה lists the חרום and several eye blemishes, and a ברייתא begins a dispute with רבי יוסי about what counts as a חרום. That dispute continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How is a real blemish different from being unequal to other כהנים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between a כהן with a real מום and a כהן who is שאינו שוה בזרעו של אהרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between a blemish and someone who is not equal among the seed of אהרן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question. Both kinds of כהנים are not allowed to do the עבודה, so what is the difference between them? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A real מום disqualifies both people and animals. Some head shapes in the משנה are not a classic מום, but they still make the כהן look different from other כהנים. If both kinds are kept out of the עבודה, the גמרא wants to know whether there is any practical difference.

keyTerms.meaning: What difference is there between (a request for a practical difference)
One who is not equal among the seed of אהרן, meaning he looks different from other כהנים

phrases.english: What difference is there between a blemish
and one who is not equal among the seed of Aaron?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין מוּמָא לְשֶׁאֵינוֹ שָׁוֶה בְּזַרְעוֹ שֶׁל אַהֲרֹן
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical difference there is between a disqualifying מום and being שאינו שוה בזרעו של אהרן.

steps.title: A real blemish profanes the service; being unequal does not
steps.stepSummary: If a כהן with a real מום does the עבודה, it becomes invalid (מחיל עבודה). If a כהן who is only שאינו שוה בזרעו של אהרן does it, the עבודה stays valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference regarding profaning the עבודה. A blemish profanes the עבודה, as the פסוק says, "He has a blemish, that he not profane." One who is not equal among the seed of אהרן does not profane the עבודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The difference is whether the עבודה the כהן did becomes profaned and invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links a מום to חילול, so a כהן with a real מום ruins the עבודה he does. A כהן who only looks different from other כהנים should not serve. But if he does serve, the עבודה stays valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Profaning the עבודה, making it invalid

steps.confusionAlert: Both kinds of כהנים are not allowed to serve. The difference here is only about what happens to the עבודה after the fact, if he served anyway.

phrases.english: There is a difference with regard to profaning the service:
a blemish profanes the service,
as it is written: "He has a blemish; that he not profane"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:23

phrases.english: one who is not equal among the seed of Aaron
does not profane the service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A real מום profanes the עבודה (based on the פסוק). Being שאינו שוה בזרעו של אהרן does not.

steps.title: How is being unequal different from a problem of appearance?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what difference there is between a כהן who is שאינו שוה בזרעו של אהרן and a כהן disqualified only because of מראית העין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between one who is not equal among the seed of אהרן and one disqualified because of how it looks?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a second, similar question. This time it compares the middle level to an even lighter one, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither of these two kinds of כהנים profanes the עבודה. So the difference found in step 2 does not help here, and the גמרא needs a new way to tell them apart.

keyTerms.meaning: How something looks to people; here, a כהן disqualified only because he seems to have a blemish

phrases.aramaic: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין שֶׁאֵינוֹ שָׁוֶה בְּזַרְעוֹ שֶׁל אַהֲרֹן,
phrases.english: What difference is there between one who is not equal among the seed of Aaron
and one disqualified due to appearance?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין שֶׁאֵינוֹ שָׁוֶה בְּזַרְעוֹ שֶׁל אַהֲרֹן וּמִשּׁוּם מַרְאִית הָעַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same question pattern as step 1, but one level lower.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical difference there is between שאינו שוה בזרעו של אהרן and מראית העין.

steps.title: Being unequal violates a positive commandment
steps.stepSummary: A כהן who is שאינו שוה בזרעו של אהרן and serves violates a עשה. A כהן disqualified only because of מראית העין does not violate a Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is a positive commandment (עשה).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers in a few words. The difference is whether serving violates a עשה from the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah wants the כהנים who serve to be equal to each other, so a כהן who looks different and serves breaks a עשה. Being kept out because of מראית העין is a rule of the חכמים, so serving breaks no Torah law. Together with step 2, this gives three levels of seriousness.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels. A real מום profanes the עבודה. שאינו שוה בזרעו של אהרן keeps the עבודה valid but violates a עשה. מראית העין is only a rule of the חכמים.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them: a positive commandment.
phrases.notes: The one who looks unequal breaks a עשה if he serves. The one with only an appearance problem does not break any Torah law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שאינו שוה בזרעו של אהרן violates a עשה; מראית העין does not.

steps.title: Explaining the pointed head and the turnip-shaped head
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defines כילון (a head shaped like a barrel cover) and לפתא (a head shaped like the top of a turnip). It then brings a ברייתא: his neck stands in the middle of his head.
steps.simpleTranslation: כילון means his head looks like a barrel cover. לפתא means his head looks like the top of a turnip. A ברייתא taught: and his neck stands in the middle of his head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now goes back to the משנה and explains what some of the head shapes it lists look like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each strange word from the משנה is compared to an everyday object so we can picture the shape. The ברייתא adds a detail about the turnip-shaped head. His head sticks out evenly around his neck, while a normal neck is at the back of the head.

keyTerms.meaning: A pointed head, shaped like a barrel cover

phrases.english: Kilon: whose head resembles the cover of a barrel,
phrases.notes: Narrow on top and wide at the bottom.

phrases.english: "Turnip-like": whose head resembles
the top of a turnip,
phrases.notes: Wide on top and narrow at the bottom, the opposite of כילון.

phrases.english: It was taught: and his neck stands in the middle of his head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section that explains the words of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כילון is a head shaped like a barrel cover. לפתא is a head shaped like a turnip top, with the neck in the middle of the head.

steps.title: Explaining the hammer head, the dent in front, and the missing piece in back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defines מקבן (a head shaped like a hammer), שקוט (a dent in the front of the head), and סקיפת (a dent in the back of the head). It explains סקיפת with a common saying: "a piece was taken."
steps.simpleTranslation: מקבן means his head looks like a hammer. "His head is שקוט" means there is a dent in the front. "סקיפת" means there is a dent in the back, as people say: "a piece was taken."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps explaining head shapes from the משנה, this time three more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שקוט and סקיפת are both dents, but in different places: שקוט is in the front and סקיפת is in the back. The word סקיפת is explained as a shortened form of the everyday phrase שקיל פיסא, "a piece was taken."

keyTerms.meaning: A hammer-shaped head, with the forehead sticking out
Dented in the back, as if a piece were missing

phrases.english: Makkavan: whose head resembles a hammer,
"And whose head is indented": in the front,
"And sekifat": in the back,
as people say: "A piece has been taken."
phrases.notes: The word סקיפת is read as a short form of שקיל פיסא, as if a piece of the back of his head is missing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the head blemishes listed in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מקבן is a hammer-shaped head. שקוט is a dent in front. סקיפת is a dent in back.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a short neck and a narrow neck
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds that a כהן whose neck is שקוט or שמוט is also disqualified. The גמרא explains that שקוט means pressed down and hidden, and שמוט means long and stretched thin.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: and his neck is short or narrow. "Short" means it is pressed down. "Narrow" means it is long and stretched out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds two neck blemishes, and then explains each word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word שקוט now describes a neck instead of a head. Here it means the neck is pushed down between the shoulders so it can hardly be seen. שמוט is the opposite: a neck that is long and thin.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא explains each head or neck blemish by comparing it to a familiar object or a common saying, so the learner can picture it.

phrases.english: It was taught: and one whose neck is short, or narrow.
"Short": whose neck is pressed down,
"Narrow": whose neck is long and drawn out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds neck blemishes from a ברייתא to the head blemishes just explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A neck that is pressed down (שקוט) or long and thin (שמוט) also disqualifies a כהן.

steps.title: Where exactly the hump dispute lies
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees a hump with a bone disqualifies. The dispute is only about a hump with no bone. The חכמים say such a כהן is אינו שוה בזרעו של אהרן, and רבי יהודה says it is just a lump of flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And those with humps, רבי יהודה etc.' If the hump has a bone in it, everyone agrees he is disqualified. They argue when it has no bone. One Sage holds that he is not equal among the seed of אהרן. The other Sage holds that it is merely a lump of flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's dispute about a כהן with a hump. It narrows the argument down to one specific case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hump with a bone in it is a real change in the body, so everyone disqualifies it. When there is no bone, the חכמים still disqualify him because he looks different from other כהנים. רבי יהודה says a lump of flesh alone is not a מום.

keyTerms.meaning: People with humps on their backs
Not like the other descendants of אהרן; he looks different from the other כהנים

steps.confusionAlert: Both 'מר סבר' lines say 'one Sage holds'. The first one is the חכמים, who disqualify. The second one is רבי יהודה, who allows him to serve.

phrases.english: And those with humps, Rabbi Yehuda etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. רבי יהודה lets them serve, and the חכמים disqualify them.

phrases.english: Where there is a bone in it,
everyone agrees that it disqualifies.
Where they disagree is where there is no bone in it:

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר — הָא אֵינוֹ שָׁוֶה בְּזַרְעוֹ שֶׁל אַהֲרֹן,
phrases.english: One Sage holds: this one is not equal among the seed of Aaron,
phrases.notes: This is the חכמים.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר — קִרְקוּרָא דְּבִישְׂרָא בְּעָלְמָא הוּא.
phrases.english: and the other Sage holds: it is merely a lump of flesh.
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִית בֵּיהּ עֶצֶם כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next case in the משנה and uses the idea of אינו שוה בזרעו של אהרן from Steps 3-4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hump with a bone disqualifies according to everyone. A boneless hump is the subject of the dispute: the חכמים disqualify him and רבי יהודה allows him to serve.

steps.title: רבא limits the bald priest rule: first version
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the משנה's קרח is someone with hair in front but none in back. If he has hair in back, he is fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'The bald one is disqualified.' רבא said: They taught this only about someone who has no hair in the back but does have hair in the front. But if he has hair in the back, he is fit. All the more so if he has hair in the back and none in the front.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains which kind of bald כהן the משנה disqualifies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hair missing in the back while there is hair in the front is unusual, so it counts as a disqualification. If there is hair in back, he is fit. Hair in back without hair in front is even more clearly fine, because that is how many men normally go bald.

keyTerms.meaning: A bald person, one missing the ring of hair around the head
They only taught this about... (a limiting phrase)

phrases.english: The bald one is disqualified.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. It means someone without a row of hair around his head from ear to ear.

phrases.english: Rava said: They taught this only

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין לוֹ לְאַחֲרָיו וְיֵשׁ לוֹ לְפָנָיו,
phrases.english: where he has none in the back but has in the front,
but if he has in the back — he is fit,
phrases.notes: He means hair in the back as well as in the front.

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ לְאַחֲרָיו וְאֵין לוֹ לְפָנָיו.
phrases.english: and all the more so where he has in the back and has none in the front.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next case in the משנה, the קרח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only someone with hair in front and none in back is disqualified as a קרח. Having hair in back makes him fit.

steps.title: רבא's limit on the bald priest: second version
steps.stepSummary: Others teach רבא's statement on the משנה's later line, 'if he has hair, he is fit'. In this version, he is fit only with hair in back and none in front. Every other case is disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach it on the later clause of the משנה: 'And if he has hair, he is fit.' רבא said: They taught this only where he has hair in the back and none in the front. But if he has hair both in the back and in the front, he is disqualified. All the more so if he has hair in the front and none in the back, or has no hair at all, he is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another version of רבא's statement. This version attaches it to a different line of the משנה and reaches a stricter result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, only the normal balding pattern, hair in back and none in front, is fit. A full ring of hair in both back and front is now disqualified. The two versions disagree about that middle case.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who teach it (another version)
The later clause of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the case of hair in both front and back. The first version calls him fit, and this second version calls him disqualified.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of רבא. Both agree that hair in back with none in front is fit. They disagree about hair in both places: fit in the first version, disqualified in the second.

phrases.english: And some teach it on the latter clause,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם יֵשׁ לוֹ — הֲרֵי זֶה כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.english: "and if he has, he is fit."
phrases.notes: These are the words of the משנה's later line: if he has the row of hair, he is fit.

phrases.english: Rava said: They taught this only

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ לְאַחֲרָיו וְאֵין לוֹ לְפָנָיו,
phrases.english: where he has in the back and has none in the front,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל יֵשׁ לוֹ בֵּין לְאַחֲרָיו בֵּין לְפָנָיו — פָּסוּל,
phrases.english: but if he has both in the back and in the front — he is disqualified,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ לְפָנָיו וְאֵין לוֹ לְאַחֲרָיו,
phrases.english: and all the more so where he has in the front and none in the back,
and one who has none at all — that he is disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version of Step 9 that attaches רבא's words to the משנה's later clause.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only hair in back with none in front is fit. Hair in both places, hair only in front, or no hair at all is disqualified.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן lists three disqualified types
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that bald כהנים, dwarves and כהנים with leaky eyes are disqualified, because they are אינו שוה בזרעו של אהרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Bald people, dwarves and people with leaky eyes are disqualified, because they are not equal among the seed of אהרן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a list of three kinds of כהנים who may not serve. He gives one reason for all three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: None of these three has a classic Torah מום. Their disqualification comes from looking different from other כהנים. This is the same idea of אינו שוה בזרעו של אהרן that was used for the hump.

keyTerms.meaning: People whose eyes constantly leak or tear

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The bald ones and the dwarves
and those with leaky eyes — are disqualified,

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵינָן שָׁוֶה בְּזַרְעוֹ שֶׁל אַהֲרֹן.
phrases.english: because they are not equal among the seed of Aaron.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הַקַּרְחָנִין וְהַנַּנָּסִין וְהַזַּבְלְגָנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement that groups together several disqualifications based on looking different.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bald כהנים, dwarves and כהנים with leaky eyes are disqualified because they are אינו שוה בזרעו של אהרן.

steps.title: Why say bald and dwarf when the משנה already teaches them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן: bald כהנים and dwarves are already listed in the משנה, so why repeat them?
steps.simpleTranslation: Bald people? We already learned that! Dwarves? We already learned that!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן needed to say two cases the משנה already taught. This sets up an answer that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא is not supposed to simply repeat a משנה. The קרח appears in our משנה, and dwarves appear in a later משנה. So part of רבי יוחנן's list seems unnecessary.

phrases.english: Bald ones — we already learned it!
phrases.notes: Our משנה said 'הקרח פסול', as seen in Step 9.

phrases.english: Dwarves — we already learned it!
phrases.notes: Dwarves are listed in a later משנה in this פרק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's statement in Step 11 as repeating the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's list of disqualified כהנים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two of the three cases are already stated in a משנה, so stating them again seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Leaky eyes are new, and the other cases are more than appearance
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן needed to teach the law of leaky-eyed כהנים. He also needed to show that bald כהנים and dwarves are not disqualified only because of מראית העין.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needed to teach us about the leaky-eyed ones. And he repeated the others, because you might have said they are disqualified only because of how it looks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 12: why does רבי יוחנן repeat cases already in the משנה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaky eyes do not appear in the משנה, so that part is new. For the bald and dwarf cases, we might have thought the disqualification is only מראית העין, meaning it just looks bad. רבי יוחנן's reason, אינו שוה בזרעו של אהרן, shows it is a real disqualification.

keyTerms.meaning: כהנים whose eyes constantly drip or leak
he needed it, it was necessary for him
lest you say, you might have thought
how it looks, a disqualification based only on appearance

phrases.english: The leaky-eyed ones, he needed to teach us,
and lest you say
[they are disqualified only] because of how it looks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New information plus clarifying the reason for the disqualification
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Bald כהנים and dwarves are disqualified only because of מראית העין.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are truly disqualified because they are אינו שוה בזרעו של אהרן, and leaky eyes are a new case.

steps.title: The משנה always says it openly when appearance is the reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: whenever the reason is only מראית העין, the משנה says so outright, as with the case of fallen eyelashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wherever the reason is how it looks, the תנא teaches it openly: 'one whose eyelashes fell out is disqualified because of how it looks.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה clearly labels appearance-only cases, like fallen eyelashes. Bald כהנים and dwarves are not labeled that way. So no one would have thought they were only מראית העין, and רבי יוחנן's statement seems unnecessary again.

keyTerms.meaning: but surely, an opening word for a challenge

phrases.english: But anywhere
that the reason is how it looks,
he teaches it openly,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording that replaces it.

phrases.english: [as it says:] 'and one whose eyelashes fell out'
'is disqualified because of how it looks'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא מִשּׁוּם מַרְאִית הָעַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that we might have thought bald כהנים and dwarves are only disqualified because of מראית העין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה openly labels appearance-only cases, and these cases have no such label, so no one would make that mistake.

steps.title: Maybe one example was meant to cover all of them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: we might have thought the משנה gave one example of מראית העין and meant it to apply to all the cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: he taught it once, and the same applies to all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its answer against the challenge in step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Perhaps the משנה mentioned מראית העין only once, with the eyelashes, but meant it for the whole list. So רבי יוחנן still needed to say that bald כהנים and dwarves are truly disqualified.

phrases.english: Lest you say:
he taught one,
phrases.notes: This means the one case labeled מראית העין, the fallen eyelashes.

phrases.english: and the same is true for all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: תָּנֵי חֲדָא, וְהוּא הַדִּין לְכוּלְּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the משנה's single label as covering the whole list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The one mention of מראית העין applies to every case in the list.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן teaches that this is not true for bald כהנים and dwarves.

steps.title: The משנה repeats the label every time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects again: the משנה does repeat 'because of how it looks' in other cases, such as missing teeth, so it does not rely on one mention.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wherever it can be repeated, he does repeat it: 'one whose teeth were removed is disqualified because of how it looks.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the answer of step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה states the label again in the case of missing teeth. So the תנא repeats it each time it applies, and one mention does not cover the whole list. This knocks out the defense in step 15, so the answer from step 13 falls away. The next step gives a new answer.

keyTerms.meaning: to repeat and teach it again

phrases.english: But anywhere that there is
[a case] to repeat and teach,
he does repeat and teach:
'and one whose teeth were removed'
phrases.notes: This line is in the next משנה, on the next page (44a).

phrases.english: 'is disqualified because of how it looks'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא מִיהְדָּר וּמִיתְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that one mention of מראית העין covers the whole list.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה repeats the label for missing teeth, so it labels each appearance-only case separately.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן is rejecting a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: Final answer: רבי יוחנן comes to reject a ברייתא that says bald, dwarf and leaky-eyed כהנים are fit by Torah law, and are disqualified only because of how it looks.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he comes to exclude a ברייתא that teaches: bald כהנים, dwarves and leaky-eyed כהנים are fit, and they were called disqualified only because of how it looks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops its earlier answer and gives a new reason for רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a ברייתא that says these כהנים are fit by Torah law and are disqualified only because of מראית העין. רבי יוחנן rules against it. He calls them truly disqualified because they are אינו שוה בזרעו של אהרן.

keyTerms.meaning: to exclude, to reject another view

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן repeats the cases from the משנה to reject the ברייתא that calls these כהנים fit by Torah law.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not let these כהנים serve. It agrees they may not serve, but only because of מראית העין. The argument is about the reason.

phrases.english: Rather, [he comes] to exclude what is taught,
as it is taught:
Bald ones, dwarves and leaky-eyed ones are fit,
and they called them disqualified
only because of how it looks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer that step 16 rejected with a new answer to step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying an opposing source that רבי יוחנן rules against
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might follow the ברייתא, which says these כהנים are fit by Torah law.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן rules they are truly disqualified, against the ברייתא.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the משנה's list alone does not tell us whether a disqualification is from the Torah or only because of appearance.

steps.title: Who is the author of this ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds the view of the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is this תנא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who wrote the ברייתא that רבי יוחנן disagrees with. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants a named author for the view that bald and similar כהנים are fit by Torah law. Knowing the author shows whose position רבי יוחנן is rejecting.

phrases.english: Who is this תנא?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the ברייתא quoted in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא of the ברייתא.

steps.title: It is רבי יהודה, who includes bald כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The author is רבי יהודה. He learns from the word 'הכהנים' in the פסוק that bald כהנים may serve.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי יהודה, as it is taught: רבי יהודה says, 'the כהנים' comes to include bald ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 18: the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reads the extra word 'הכהנים' as including bald כהנים in the עבודה. So by Torah law they are fit. This matches his view in step 8 that a hump without a bone is just flesh.

keyTerms.meaning: 'the כהנים', the word in the פסוק that he learns from

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, who says bald כהנים are fit by Torah law. רבי יוחנן rules against him.

phrases.english: It is רבי יהודה, as it is taught:
רבי יהודה says:
'The כהנים' comes to include the bald ones.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:8

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא is רבי יהודה, who uses 'הכהנים' to include bald כהנים.

steps.title: The משנה's first definition of a גבן: no eyebrows
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a כהן with no eyebrows, or with only one, is the גבן the Torah lists among blemished כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a כהן has no eyebrows, or has only one eyebrow, that is the גבן mentioned in the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens by defining the word גבן from the list of blemished כהנים in the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah lists 'גבן' as a blemish that disqualifies a כהן from serving. The first opinion in the משנה says the word refers to the eyebrows: a כהן who has none, or has only one.

keyTerms.meaning: A blemish in the Torah's list (ויקרא 21:20); this opinion says it is about the eyebrows

phrases.english: MISHNA: If he has no eyebrows,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא גְּבִין אֶחָד —
phrases.english: or he has only one eyebrow,
that is the gibben stated in the Torah.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:20

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the earlier discussion of רבי יהודה and the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן lacking eyebrows, or having only one, is the Torah's גבן

steps.title: Two other definitions: flat eyebrows or two spines
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסא says a גבן has eyebrows that lie flat. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says a גבן has two backs and two spines.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי דוסא says: a גבן is one whose eyebrows lie flat. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says: it is one who has two backs and two spines.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings two more opinions about what the word גבן means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי דוסא still connects the word to eyebrows, but he means eyebrows so long that they droop over the eyes. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס connects it to the back ('גב'), and this view is challenged later in the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: Lying down, here meaning drooping flat

phrases.english: Rabbi Dosa says:
One whose eyebrows lie flat.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the corrected word, in square brackets, means 'his eyebrows'.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus says:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שְׁנֵי גַּבִּין וּשְׁתֵּי שִׁדְרָאוֹת.
phrases.english: One who has two backs and two spines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives other opinions on the same definition
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי דוסא: drooping eyebrows. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס: two backs and two spines.

steps.title: A ברייתא says גבן means many eyebrows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה. A ברייתא says גבן means many eyebrows, and it learns the case of missing eyebrows from the extra word 'או'.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Does גבן really mean one who has no eyebrows? Contrast this with a ברייתא: 'גבן' is one who has many eyebrows. Where do we learn about one who has no eyebrows, or only one? The פסוק says 'או גבן', 'or a גבן'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets the משנה against a ברייתא that seems to define גבן in the opposite way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the word גבן itself means no eyebrows. The ברייתא says the word means many eyebrows, and that no eyebrows is only added through the word 'או'. So the two sources seem to contradict each other about the plain meaning of the word.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And contrast them': introduces a source that contradicts
'The פסוק teaches': introduces the verse used as a source

phrases.english: GEMARA: But does 'gibben' mean one who has none?
And contrast it with this:
'Gibben' means one who has many eyebrows.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לוֹ גְּבִינִין, אוֹ אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא גְּבִין אַחַד — מִנַּיִן?
phrases.english: One who has no eyebrows, or has only one eyebrow: from where do we know?
The verse states: 'Or a gibben.'
phrases.notes: The extra word 'או' ('or') is what brings in the case of missing eyebrows.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the first definition in the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's claim that the word גבן itself means no eyebrows
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says the word means many eyebrows and learns no eyebrows only from 'או'.

steps.title: רבא: the משנה means it is learned from 'או גבן'
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the משנה does not say the word גבן means no eyebrows. It means that this case is learned from the extra words 'או גבן'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is learned from the extra words 'או גבן'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the contradiction by reading the משנה in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'זהו גבן האמור בתורה' is now read as 'this is included by the Torah's phrase או גבן', and not as the plain meaning of the word. This way the משנה agrees with the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching learned from how the words of a פסוק are expounded

steps.whatToRemember: No eyebrows is a blemish, but it is learned from the extra word 'או' in 'או גבן'. The plain word גבן means many eyebrows.

phrases.english: Rava said:
This is the exposition of 'or a gibben.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא זֶהוּ מִדְרָשׁ אוֹ גִּבֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from the ברייתא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to define the word גבן itself as no eyebrows.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means that no eyebrows is learned from the phrase 'או גבן', which matches the ברייתא.

steps.title: A creature with two spines cannot live
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס. רב ruled that a creature with two backs and two spines does not count as a living offspring, so how can it be a living כהן?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'רבי דוסא says, etc.' Is this to say that such a person can live? But it was taught: if a woman or animal miscarries a creature with two backs and two spines, רב said that for a woman it is not counted as a child, and for an animal it is forbidden to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next part of the משנה and attacks the two-spines definition, using a ruling of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב treats a two-spined creature as one that cannot survive. A woman who gives birth to it does not have the laws of a birth, and an animal born like this is forbidden to eat. If so, there could never be a living כהן with two spines, so how could רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס say this is the Torah's גבן?

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is this to say that it lives?'
It is not counted as a child

phrases.english: 'Rabbi Dosa says,' etc.
Is this to say that he can live?
But it was stated:
One who miscarries a creature

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ שְׁנֵי גַּבִּין וּשְׁתֵּי שִׁדְרָאוֹת,
phrases.english: that has two backs and two spines,
and Rav said:
In a woman, it is not considered an offspring;
in an animal, it is forbidden to eat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first definition to רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס's definition
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס's definition: two backs and two spines
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב ruled such a creature cannot live, so it cannot describe a living כהן with a blemish.

steps.title: רב: he means a crooked spine
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר חייא had already asked רב this question. רב answered that רבי חנינא means a crooked spine that only looks like two.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר חייא already raised this contradiction to רב, and רב said to him: 'Are you שימי?!' Rather, he means one whose spine is crooked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by bringing רב's own reply when he was asked the very same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס did not mean two actual spines. He meant a spine so crooked that it looks like two. A person like this can live, but the blemish disqualifies him from service, so there is no contradiction with רב's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He already raised this contradiction to him'

steps.whatToRemember: The 'two backs and two spines' of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס is not literal. It means a crooked spine, which a living person can have.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'שימי את!' as a ruling. It is just רב's sharp reaction to the question. The actual answer is the line that comes after it: a crooked spine.

phrases.english: This contradiction was already raised to him
by Rav Shimi bar Ḥiyya, to Rav,
and he said to him: Are you Shimi?!
phrases.notes: רב is reacting with surprise that רב שימי, his own grandson, would ask this. It is not part of the answer itself.

phrases.english: Rather, it is where his spine is crooked.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּבָר רְמָא נִיהֲלֵיהּ רַב שִׁימִי בַּר חִיָּיא לְרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רב's ruling
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: not a literal reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חנינא meant a person with two actual spines, who could not live.
steps.terutzMaskana: He meant a crooked spine that looks like two. Such a person lives but is blemished.

steps.title: The משנה defines a חרום
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a חרום is disqualified. It defines him as someone who can paint both eyes in one stroke.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A חרום is disqualified. Who is a חרום? Someone who can paint both of his eyes at once.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a new blemish, the חרום. It gives a simple test for who counts as one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the nose sticks out between the eyes. So you cannot paint both eyes with one brushstroke. If the nose is so sunk that the brush passes straight across both eyes, the כהן is a חרום and may not do the עבודה.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with a sunken nose; one of the blemishes listed in the Torah
Disqualified (here: from doing the Temple service)

phrases.english: Mishnah:
The ḥarum is disqualified.
Who is a ḥarum?
One who can paint both of his eyes at once.
phrases.notes: His nose is so sunk that one brushstroke goes right across both eyes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of the גבן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חרום is disqualified. A חרום is one who can paint both eyes in a single stroke.

steps.title: The משנה lists eye blemishes
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists eye problems that disqualify a כהן. It adds that missing eyelashes disqualify only because of how it looks.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both eyes too high, both eyes too low, one eye high and one low, or seeing the downstairs room and the upstairs at once. Also one who cannot look at the sun, one with mismatched eyes, and one whose eyes always tear. And one whose eyelashes fell out is disqualified because of how it looks.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a list of eye blemishes, all of which disqualify a כהן. The last case, missing eyelashes, works differently from the rest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most items here are real blemishes: eyes in the wrong place, unusual sight, or eyes that differ from each other or always tear. Losing your eyelashes is not a real blemish. The כהן is still disqualified, because to onlookers it looks like a blemish (מראית העין).

keyTerms.meaning: Those who cannot look at the sun
One whose two eyes look different from each other
One whose eyes tear all the time

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think missing eyelashes is a full Torah blemish like the others. It disqualifies only because it looks like one.

phrases.english: If both his eyes are set high,
or both his eyes are set low,

phrases.aramaic: עֵינוֹ אַחַת לְמַעְלָה וְעֵינוֹ אַחַת לְמַטָּה,
phrases.english: or one eye is high and one eye is low,

phrases.aramaic: רוֹאֶה אֶת הַחֶדֶר וְאֶת הָעֲלִיָּיה כְּאֶחָד,
phrases.english: or he sees the room and the upper story at the same time,
those who cannot look at the sun, one with mismatched eyes, and one whose eyes always tear,
and one whose eyelashes have fallen out —
is disqualified because of how it looks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with more blemishes, now of the eyes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These eye blemishes disqualify a כהן. Missing eyelashes disqualify only because of מראית העין.

steps.title: A ברייתא learns other nose blemishes from 'או חרום'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא defines חרום as a sunken nose. It learns other nose problems from the word 'או'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: חרום means his nose is sunk. If his nose is short and turned up, blocked, or drooping, how do we know he is blemished? The פסוק says 'Or a חרום'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a ברייתא that explains the word חרום. It then stretches the blemish to cover other kinds of nose problems.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain word חרום means a sunken nose. The extra word 'או' (or) in the פסוק adds other nose blemishes: too short, blocked, or too long. We saw the same move with 'או' earlier for the גבן.

phrases.english: Gemara: The Sages taught:
"Ḥarum" means one whose nose is sunken.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:18

phrases.english: If his nose is short and turned up, or his nose is blocked,
or his nose droops, from where do we know he is blemished?
The verse says: "Or a ḥarum."
phrases.notes: The extra word 'or' brings in all these other nose problems.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא starts on the משנה with a ברייתא that defines and widens the חרום blemish.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sunken nose is חרום. Short, blocked, or drooping noses are also blemishes, learned from 'או'.

steps.title: רבי יוסי limits חרום
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says the only חרום is one who can paint both eyes at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: A חרום is only someone who can paint both of his eyes at once.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי disagrees with the first opinion in the ברייתא. He limits the blemish to the single case in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion counted many kinds of nose blemishes. רבי יוסי says only the extreme sunken nose counts, the one where a single stroke paints both eyes. His words match the wording of our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is only...', a phrase that limits a definition

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
A "ḥarum" is only
one who can paint both of his eyes at once.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר אֵין חָרוּם אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a narrower, opposing definition to the first opinion in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only one who can paint both eyes in a single stroke is a חרום.

steps.title: The חכמים say רבי יוסי went too far
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים object that רבי יוסי has gone too far.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: You have gone too far.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back against רבי יוסי's narrow definition. The sentence goes on past this point, so this step sets up their reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים attack רבי יוסי's view as too extreme. In their view, his test leaves out cases that should count. Their full explanation comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: You have gone too far, you exaggerated

phrases.english: They said to him: You have gone too far,
phrases.notes: They mean his definition is too narrow; their reason continues right after this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוסי's narrow definition from step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's view that only one who paints both eyes at once is a חרום
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His test is so extreme that it leaves out cases that should count as חרום.
